alt: Windows 11 performance comparison graphic showing RAM usage before and after Microsoft freed nearly 900MB previously consumed by its own force-installed apps including Defender, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365
story: At Ignite 2026 in November, Microsoft admitted its own background apps — Defender, OneDrive, Purview, and Microsoft 365 — were collectively consuming 860MB of RAM on Windows 11 PCs without users knowing; Copilot itself uses up to 1GB idle while advertising the ability to diagnose why your PC runs slowly; Microsoft has since freed that memory and is removing force-installed Copilot-heavy Microsoft 365 apps from enterprise Windows 11, saying they 'came at a very high cost' — weeks after telling users that 8GB RAM is 'a great fit for everyday Windows 11 use.'
why_funny: Windows 11's AI health tool, advertised as diagnosing why your PC runs slowly, was itself running on a gigabyte of silently-installed Microsoft bloatware — the patient was the doctor.
